title: Stoker metadata — release
description: `games/<gameId>/releases/<id>.json`: one version of a game as people name it ("1.4.2"), and every known build of it — the files' fingerprint, how to install and start them on each platform, and the fixes they need. One file per release, so a new version is a new file and never a conflict in an old one. The game's files are never in the repository: an instance matches its own copy to a build here by the build's fingerprint.

name.description: The version as its publisher names it, or a store's build id until somebody knows better. Unique within the game.

order.description: Higher is newer, across channels, so "newest" has one answer. Recorded, not derived: "1.10" sorts before "1.9" as text, and a Steam build id says nothing about a GOG version. Gaps are fine — a release inserted between two takes a number between them.

channel.description: `stable` is what a player gets by default. `beta` is a pre-release branch, never offered as the latest or as an update.

branch.description: The pre-release branch a beta is on — `beta`, `experimental` — which is what a player who installed it follows. Absent means `beta`.

releasedAt.description: When the publisher released it, where a store says. Not when anybody ingested it.

steamApiFileNames.description: File names, besides `steam_api(64).dll` and `libsteam_api.so`, that this release loads its Steam API from — a GOG port that renamed it. Per release, because the port and the Steam release of one game are two releases and only one has it.

settings.description: This release's own answer to the game's settings. Absent fields take the game's.

hooks.description: Replaces the game's rules whole — rule lists are never merged, because two lists hooking one export have no meaningful order. `{ "hooks": [] }` switches the game's off for this release.

plugins.description: Plugins for this release. Each replaces the game's assignment of the same plugin — `enabled: false` to switch it off here — and the game's others still apply.

fixes.description: Patches and mods for this release's copies — applied after a build's own fixes and before the game's — to whichever copies their `when` holds for.

disableFixes.description: The game's fixes, by id, that must not be applied to this release's copies even where their `when` holds.

build.description: One copy of the release's files: the platforms they run on and everything that says how to install and start them there. A build serving Windows and Linux from one set of files is one build with a launch per platform. A release has a build per copy of it anybody has described — the Steam depots, the GOG installer, a disk copy — so several builds may cover the same platform; what tells them apart is their files, and no two builds of a game have the same fingerprint.

id.description: Stable, so a fix or a report can name the build. An instance keeps its own build ids; it records which repository build its copy is.

language.description: The one language this build is, when it is only one — GOG ships an installer per language for many titles, and those are builds of one release. Absent when it carries every language it supports.

sources.description: Every place these exact files are known to come from, with that place's own ids. Usually one; more when stores ship identical files — a DRM-free game whose Steam depots and GOG installer unpack to the same tree is one build with two sources, since what a build is is its files.

content.description: The fingerprint of the build's files as ingested: the installer's contents, the depot tree, the directory. Absent only for a build described before anybody ingested it.

markers.description: Files that identify the build when its fingerprint does not: a copy is this build when every marker is there with its bytes. A copy is matched first by its sources (for Steam, its depot manifests), then by its fingerprint, then by markers. Choose files nothing writes to — the executables, the main data archives — and enough of them that no other build of the game has them all.

launches.description: The ways to start it, in the order a launcher lists them.

integrations.description: Every place the build links a store SDK, and what the install does there. Many per build: games ship a copy of the library beside every executable, and patching only the first leaves the rest talking to the store.

dependencies.description: Runtimes the machine needs, in install order — order matters, as runtimes have install-order requirements. A runtime for another platform than the one being installed is skipped.

selectionGroups.description: Questions an install asks — which language, which optional content — whose answers are fixes.

fixes.description: What is done to this copy, in order, before its release's and its game's fixes: the publisher's setup, its languages and DLC, its unpacked executables, and patches that only this copy needs. The stored build is never edited; every change is a fix or a setting.

disableFixes.description: Fixes of the release or the game, by id, that must not be applied to this build even where their `when` holds.

installScripts.description: The Steam `installscript.vdf` files the build carries, as the publisher wrote them: the evidence its `setup` steps were read from.

compatibility.description: How the build runs under Stoker, per platform, as somebody found it. The record a fix is judged by.

notes.description: About this copy — a repack, a regional installer. Markdown.

buildSource.description: One place the files come from, with that place's own ids: what "is there a newer build upstream" compares against, and the first thing a copy is matched by.

oneOf.description: A Steam build is matched by its depots, never by `buildId` alone: one build id covers every depot of a branch — Windows, Linux, each language — and so belongs to several builds here. A copy is this build when its depot manifests are exactly these.

appId.description: When the depots are another app's than the game's own.

depots.description: Depot id to manifest id — what the files are. Steam's per-file SHA-1s are in those manifests and nowhere else.

versionName.description: GOG's version name, shared across operating systems.

files.description: The installer's files — `setup_game_1.4.2.exe` and its `.bin` parts — so somebody holding one can tell whether it is this build.

version.description: The title version the package carries.

oneOf.description: A directory taken as it was, or files recorded by hand.

key.description: What fixes and settings refer to it by: `play`, `configure`. Unique per platform within the build; the same key on two platforms is the same launch for each.

executable.description: The program to start — for a console build, the image the emulator is given.

workingDirectory.description: Absent means the executable's own folder.

default.description: The one Play starts. At most one per platform.

provider.description: `none` records a site examined and found to be nothing Stoker answers.

architecture.description: Which build of the library the file is. `steam_api.dll` and `steam_api64.dll` are different binaries, and the wrong one in their place is a game that will not start and says nothing.

path.description: Where the library is, or goes: `Binaries/Win64/steam_api64.dll`. For Ren'Py the loader script, for Godot the `override.cfg`.

action.description: `replace` the shipped library with Stoker's; `add` one the build lacks; `leave` it as recorded and deliberately untouched.

originalBlake3.description: What must be found before patching — BLAKE3, which the instance's manifest already holds for the file. A file that hashes otherwise has been modified or mis-identified, and the patch is refused.

shippedLibraryVersion.description: The SDK version as found in the build: `1.59`.

requiredLibraryVersion.description: The SDK version Stoker's library has to satisfy.

interfaceVersions.description: The Steamworks interface versions to answer with — `SteamFriends015` — for a site whose own library names none (a GOG layer, a store's own `steam_api`). Read from another file that does: Valve's original kept beside it, the Steam release's copy, the executable.

interfaceVersionsFrom.description: The file `interfaceVersions` was read from, and the build it is in when that is not this one.

providerAppId.description: The id the build reports to the store, when it is not the game's own: a regional SKU, a bundled demo, a development AppId left in a shipping binary.

writeAppIdFile.description: Write `steam_appid.txt` beside the library; a Steamworks game refuses to initialise outside a Steam client without one.

enabled.description: False to keep the finding without applying it.

key.description: Stable machine name, e.g. `language`. Installs answer by it, so it never changes once published.

prompt.description: What the installer shows above the choices.

required.description: The install refuses to go ahead without an answer. False with a default is the usual shape.

buildFix.description: A fix of one build. Besides patches and mods, a build's fixes are what make the copy what it is: its `setup`, its `languagePack`s and `dlc`, its `unpacked` executables.

dlcId.description: For a `dlc` fix, which of the game's DLC (`dlc/<dlcId>.json`) it is — what tells the store's "is this DLC installed?" the truth.

selectionGroup.description: The question this fix answers, by key. Absent: not one of a question's answers.

allOf.description: Only a DLC whose content already ships in the build's files — the game unlocks it by asking whether it is owned — has nothing to do.
An `unpacked` fix only unpacks, and unpacking is only ever such a fix.

steamBuildId.description: The Steam build the script was read from, when it is not this build's own.

status.description: `works`: played through a session. `starts`: reaches its window, not yet played. `crashes`: the last attempt failed. `untested`: nobody has tried. The same scale a Stoker instance computes from its run reports.

runner.description: What it was run through when that is not the platform itself: `proton-9.0`, an emulator's name and version.

verified.description: The day it was last found so.
